label.claim_answered: Whether men should have a say in abortion or automatically pay full child support for unwanted children
label.reason: Mixed rule: answers central claims about both sexes' reproductive rights and obligations, proposing a compromise rather than defending one sex.

reviewers.claim_answered: A man should remain fully financially responsible for a child even after clearly opting out of parenthood
reviewers.reason: Argues fathers should be able to limit parental obligations when the mother alone decides to continue the pregnancy; also weighs both parents’ interests.

reviewers.claim_answered: Men should have equal say in abortion; men must pay for children they never wanted
reviewers.reason: Answers both the pro-men claim for equal say and the anti-men child-support obligation; proposes a compromise

reviewers.claim_answered: Should men have equal say in abortion and pay child support even if they don't want a child
reviewers.reason: He rejects equal male say in abortion and automatic full child support, balancing women's autonomy with men's opt-out

reviewers.claim_answered: A man who clearly rejected fatherhood early should be able to opt out of child support
reviewers.reason: Weighs abortion and paternal obligation for both parents without blaming either sex; policy framing could also read as politics

reviewers.claim_answered: Men should automatically be financially responsible for a child they never wanted
reviewers.reason: Argues men should have legal options to opt out of parental obligations when women have sole choice over pregnancy
